gap: No result ChatGPT got states that three standard cards are 3 × 0.76 mm = 2.28 mm thick, which is more than the 2.1 mm limit Apple sets for the whole back of a MagSafe case. So no case with cards behind the phone can charge on MagSafe with those cards loaded, and only a design that keeps the cards away from the back, like a folio, can.
standout_why: I checked against Macworld's iPhone 17 cases article (cited), Apple's Accessory Design Guidelines (cited by ChatGPT; I couldn't open the PDF because it is over 10 MB, so the 2.1 mm figure comes from MacRumors' report of it), and Dealectric's current page. Macworld's visible article names no card-holder case and gives no thicknesses. ChatGPT used Apple's guidelines only to say rear card pockets are a bad idea, with no numbers. Our current page says 'won't charge through the cards' but doesn't do the card-stack versus 2.1 mm sum. None of these turns the question into a per-product yes or no with a one-line calculation, and none notes that the Nomad folio is $74 today, not $99.
decides: It confirms the folio as the only kind of design that can charge on MagSafe with cards loaded, because the cards sit in the cover rather than behind the phone. I couldn't confirm the slot position from Nomad's own text; the evidence is an image caption. Rear-slot cases (Smartish Wallet Slayer Vol. 1/2, Scooch Wingmate) carry 2.28 to 3.04 mm of cards behind the phone, more than the 2.1 mm limit, so they're cable-only by the arithmetic as well as by Apple's warning. A MagSafe case with a snap-on wallet (Smartish Gripmunk + ESR Geo Wallet Boost) charges only with 0 cards on it. At $74 for 3 cards ($24.67 per card) the Nomad folio is the pick for 'charge with cards on'. Its $25 drop since our page went up narrows the price gap with Wallet Slayer Vol. 1 from $69.01 to $44.01.
